question.text: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the vapour pressure of a solution containing <math><mn>1</mn></math> mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> -hexane and <math><mn>3</mn></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> -heptane is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>550</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hg</mi></math>. At the same temperature, if one more mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> -heptane is added to this solution, the vapour pressure of the solution increases by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hg</mi></math>. What is the vapour pressure in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mmHg</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> - heptane in its pure state______?

solution.text:
Ptotal=P∘hexane. Xhexane+P∘heptane.Xheptane

550=P∘hexane×14+P∘heptane×34     ..(i)

After mixing 1 mole n-heptane

560=P∘hexane×15+P∘heptane×45     .....(ii)

On solving eq. (i) and (ii)

P∘heptane=600 mm of Hg
